when: stale approval
agent retry after cancel

A team voted to approve policy D1 but D2 is enforced later; how do we distinguish the original agreement from present authorization?
社内の承認から手続きが変わったのに、前の合意を今の実行許可として使える？
routes.plain_meaning: A cancelled old AI job must not silently change the budget or answer of work happening now, merely because the old record still exists. Likewise, a past human approval and a lost external acknowledgement do not prove whether payment, email, or another effect actually committed; an unknown outcome is not fresh authority to execute again.

when: Qwen Code resume after conversation-only rewind
retained file snapshot identity collision
malformed numeric turn ordinal
routes.plain_meaning: A past AI coding turn can disappear from the conversation while its file backup still exists. If the next turn accidentally reuses the old backup's ID, a normal rollback choice may restore the wrong file. Preserve the old ID, reject malformed IDs, and prove the replacement is safe.

when: Anthropic system prompt cache_control
five system messages with cache_idx 4
Anthropic cache breakpoints per request
routes.plain_meaning: When an AI prompt is assembled from five cached instruction messages, placing a cache marker on each fragment can exceed the provider's request limit. The upstream developer changed it to one marker on the last applicable system instruction, preserving explicitly marked cache boundaries and verifying two small before/after cases.

when: native function-calling tool result confused with executor error
tool payload contains __cuga_fc_error__ as ordinary data
CUGA Lite sandbox tool error provenance
routes.plain_meaning: An AI tool can return ordinary data that happens to contain the word 'error'. That does not mean running the tool failed. After a specific GitHub review, the CUGA implementer changed the adapter to check its own outcome channel instead of trusting a label inside the returned data, and added one successful-result and one real-exception regression.

when: Cerebras max_tokens and max_completion_tokens both included
LlamaIndex Cerebras additional_kwargs overrides
Cerebras OpenAI-compatible output cap alias precedence
routes.plain_meaning: An AI request can accidentally give two different answers to the question 'how long may the output be?' because an older option and its replacement are both present. A standalone, offline checker spots the clash in already-built JSON request data, while the proposed upstream test pinpoints where to remove the extra key.

when: LlamaIndex ChatMessage legacy images silently disappear on JSON restore
ImageDocument serialized dictionaries and ImageBlock migration
chat history image round-trip duplicate or byte-less husk
routes.plain_meaning: A coding assistant can say 'the message was restored' while silently forgetting where an attached image was stored. In this LlamaIndex source review, the developer changed the loader so recoverable image references survive and already-present images are not duplicated; the fix cannot recreate picture bytes that the saved file never contained. A separate five-case local check is available for someone using the actual package.

when: AI denies a grant/benefit in a hypothetical pilot; no clear appeal path
AI-assisted adverse decision review or dispute escalation
retain legacy remedy during non-enforcing transition
A scholarship application was rejected by an automated screen; how can the applicant see reasons, correct records and reach a human?
AIで不採用や給付不認定になった。誤った情報の訂正と人間への異議申立て経路をどう確かめる？
routes.plain_meaning: If an AI flags your application as incomplete, you should be able to find out why, correct an error and reach a responsible person without losing existing avenues of redress; the mock worksheet cannot prove those protections exist in real life. A seven-question offline human-readable worksheet now lets a reader generate a practical clarification memo, without proving the remedy exists.

when: A cloud-hosted and local/self-hosted AI agent are advertised as separate paths but share an undisclosed control-plane gate
Qwen Code dual-path Managed Agent Hosted versus local M6 acceptance question
does no cross-engine fallback prove independent operability
Our local employee workflow and external cloud workflow share the same sign-in server; are they truly independent fallbacks?
社内ツールとクラウドの2系統が同じログイン障害で止まる。独立した選択肢と言える？
routes.plain_meaning: Two buttons labeled 'cloud' and 'local' do not necessarily mean two independent choices. If the cloud's login or control plane is unavailable, can the local path still start and recover its own AI task? Qwen's design owner accepted Nakagawa Master's proposal to test that distinction, but those tests are not yet evidence of a shipped independent product.
routes.original_relation: Source-context only; read the detailed route's exact fit/causality boundaries before claiming use of a specific original theory. Cross-domain organization/continuity example: compare nominal two-path choice with effective independent access, exit and recovery when a common authentication chokepoint fails. This is a conditional analogy with the original non-ownership / effective-domination analysis; a shared login alone is not proof of domination.

when: an AI agent can change its own approval mode from ask to auto
does reversing a configuration change make granting tool authority safe
independent author adopted an agent self-authorization invariant in their published manuscript
routes.plain_meaning: Even if an AI can undo a change from 'ask a human' to 'run automatically', it may already have done new things before undoing it. Nakagawa Master made that distinction concrete in another author's agent-design manuscript; the author then wrote and merged a new sixth condition, and reused the condition in a second document. That is documented human editorial adoption, not proof that all AI products or readers are safe.

when: Qwen ACP agent team tool permission prompted twice when same manager is notified twice
AI teammate approvals distinguished only by agent name and millisecond timestamp
fake event emitter uses Set and masks duplicate listener registrations
routes.plain_meaning: When an AI teammate leaves, its old permission request can still occupy the next teammate's approval slot. Nakagawa Master identified a viable child-to-bridge notification route after the independent reviewer reproduced the stuck record. The receiving developer publicly corrected his own SDK assertion, said Nakagawa was right, and implemented a versioned retirement notification with focused component tests; the same open Qwen PR also contains separately adopted listener-idempotence and unique-approval-ID corrections. Original theory can be compared through canonical source; the developer has not claimed adopting the whole theory corpus.

when: a multi-team Contract owner leaves the team but the existing signed Contract remains in force
an AI/governance assistant must distinguish who may approve Contract revisions from whether parties still must honor the current version
a successor Contract owner is selected and pending revisions must not become approved merely from succession
routes.plain_meaning: When the person appointed to approve contract changes leaves the group, the existing agreement does not disappear. The groups can still follow their previously approved agreement; the former approver cannot approve new amendments. Nakagawa Master proposed this distinction to an outside author, who independently narrowed what must stop and integrated four new rules into their EAA draft branch. The separate published agent-design chapter was also updated by the same author; no fresh reader scale is proven. A follow-on receiving-author PR #108 now proposes a source-linked approval/application record and names Nakagawa Master as the original outside proposer while separately identifying the actual document proposer and human approver; that ledger PR was merged into the author's working branch and does not independently prove the approver's private decision.
